* fix(tests): the seniority cache cleanup names both globals, not one

CI went red on six tests this slice never touched: "Head of Year 5" came
back DIRECTOR, "Lead Generation Executive" came back SENIOR. Reproduced
locally by running tests/test_seniority_detector.py and
tests/test_slice5_fixes.py together - 6 failed - and green again with the
one-line fix below.

detect_seniority reads TWO module-level caches, _seniority_terms and
_seniority_noise. TestMissingDataFileDegradesGracefully repoints _DATA at a
missing directory and calls detect_seniority, so BOTH get populated from the
broken path - but its autouse fixture only ever cleared the first. The noise
pattern stayed cached as None for the rest of the session, every later
detect_seniority skipped noise stripping, and the trap phrases fired as real
seniority claims.

That is precisely the session poisoning the fixture's own docstring was
written to prevent, one cache over. It hid because some earlier file in the
full suite happened to warm the noise cache from the real data first;
deleting twenty LLM-only test files in slice B removed the accident and the
latent bug surfaced. Local subset runs never see it - the order differs.

Clearing both, before and after, makes the class hermetic whatever runs
around it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011wAduRqokWdPEByUkcVbvc

* fix(prod): stop injecting the four dead LLM keys into the backend container

The security review caught what the rest of this slice missed: deleting the
provider pool from the code does not take the credentials out of the running
container. docker-compose.prod.yml still mapped GEMINI_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY,
CEREBRAS_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY into the backend's environment, so the
process kept holding four live keys that no code path can spend.

That is pure blast radius. A credential an application cannot use is worth
nothing to the product and everything to anyone who reaches the process, and
it is the kind of leftover that survives for months because nothing breaks
when it is wrong.

.env.example now says DELETE them rather than "nothing reads them" - the
second sentence was true of the code and still left the key sitting in a
deployed environment. Railway's backend service needs the same four removed
by hand; that is the owner's step, named in the PR body.

feat(drills): every drill must be able to go red — negative controls in the registry (#598)

A drill that exits 0 proves the drill RAN. It has never proved the guard could
still go RED, and this registry made the second claim while measuring only the
first. A blinded checker exits 0 exactly like a working one: all([]) is True, a
derivation that resolves to zero files prints zero lines and succeeds, and an
assertion that holds for the wrong reason still holds. Both of those shipped
here inside one PR, and both were found only by breaking the guard on purpose.

WHAT A NEGATIVE CONTROL IS
A `drilled` guard now declares a second command, `negative`: argv run from ROOT
that BLINDS or BREAKS the guard deliberately, and must therefore exit NON-ZERO.
`chain_check.py --drill --break-checker W1` switches one check off;
`doc_sync_mutation_test.py --blind` runs the whole mutation harness with the
mutation NOT applied. The runner now demands BOTH on every sweep: drill exit 0
AND negative exit non-zero = proven. A negative that exits 0 is reported RED
("THE DRILL CANNOT GO RED"), whatever the registry claims about itself.

THE COUNT, HONESTLY
4 guards have a negative control: chain_check.py, gate_wiring_check.py,
doc_sync_check.py (via the mutation harness's new --blind) and drill_registry.py
itself. 25 are owed — 5 declared owed as before, plus 20 `drilled` guards that
declare no negative. Those 20 are NOT red: a guard that cannot express a
mutation is honestly owed, and a bar that reds twenty guards the day it lands is
a bar someone switches off inside a week. Each states in one line what would
have to be built (they hardcode their cases inline, so there is nothing a flag
can switch off from outside; merge_cage.py would need a --break-checker inside a
3,600-line self_drill, check_workflow_slack_wiring.py already spends ~300
`bash -n` spawns a pass). Silence is not allowed: `drilled` with neither a
negative nor a reason is MALFORMED, for the same reason `owed` needs a reason.

--count-owed is unchanged and still prints 5. Its meaning is now written into
its own description: DECLARED DEBT, NOT PROOF OF LIVENESS. A guard missing from
that count may still have a drill that cannot go red. The two numbers are
printed side by side and never folded into one, so the ratchet in merge_cage.py
reads exactly what it read before.

THE REGISTRY HOLDS ITSELF TO IT
`--break-checker UNDECLARED|BROKEN|STALE|MALFORMED` blinds one of this file's
own rules; its self-drill must then fail. All four verified exit 1. The
self-drill grew from 8 cases to 13: a negative that exits 0 is reported red, a
negative that cannot be launched is reported (never assumed fine), a `drilled`
guard with no negative reads OWED and stays quiet, one with no negative AND no
reason is MALFORMED, and the happy path (drill green + negative red) is accepted
silently — a bar nothing can clear is an outage, not a bar.

ci.yml: `--run-drills` already runs every guard's negative, because the runner
does. The registry's own is skipped there (a drill may not invoke itself), so it
runs as its own step next to `--drill`.

Also removes an unused `sys` import in scripts/ruleset_gate.py so `ruff check
scripts` is green; its drill still passes 16/16.

Verified from the repo root:

  drill_registry.py --drill             13/13, exit 0
  --drill --break-checker <each of 4>   exit 1 (the drill can go red)
  --run-drills                          every drill and every negative pass;
                                        the only failure is the Windows-only
                                        DRILL TIMEOUT on check_workflow_slack_

  --count-owed                          5 (unchanged)
  chain_check.py --no-map               exit 0

  doc_sync_check.py                     no drift
  gen_doc_blocks.py --check             current

fix(arm): merge with the owner's token so a machine merge wakes main (#593)

Measured 2026-09-19 across every merge since 09-16: the 8 merges made by
github-actions (#578 #580 #579 #584 #586 #589 #591 and the Dependabot
sweep's) started ZERO workflows on main -- no CI, no CodeQL, no

started all five. GitHub's rule: an event caused by GITHUB_TOKEN creates no
workflow run, and a merge queued or made by GITHUB_TOKEN is such an event.

run for the merges it exists for.

`secrets.MERGE_TOKEN` (owner's fine-grained PAT: Contents R/W + Pull
requests R/W, this repo only) with GITHUB_TOKEN as the fallback, and say
loudly on every run when the secret is missing.

   (09:35, 13:21, 16:45, 19:05). auto-merge.yml now also wakes on `status`
